variants.name: Current unlimited captures
variants.review: Good foundation. Reply-aware play already beats word-only play; the game is not devoid of strategy.

variants.name: Classic three-capture cap
variants.review: Useful control. Less attacking than unlimited captures; no clear reason to restore the cap.

variants.name: Land 2 / castles 5
variants.review: Best first scoring playtest: ordinary land 2, castles 5. More meaningful word sacrifices; watch final-reply advantage.

variants.name: Castles worth 6
variants.review: Simple and readable objectives, but less broad territory play than raising ordinary land.

variants.name: Gentler length bonus
variants.review: Helps exhaustive solvers more than limited-attention players; reduces the delight of long words.

variants.name: Every held tile earns 1
variants.review: Holding income overwhelms word points in the limited-attention model.

variants.name: Holding income capped at 4
variants.review: Adds recurring accounting but often saturates early, changing totals more than decisions.

variants.name: Held castles earn 2
variants.review: Tangible defense incentive; sizable income and weaker comeback signal.

variants.name: Castles earn 3 after two rounds
variants.review: Waiting longer adds bookkeeping and can deepen leads.

variants.name: Two home jokers
variants.review: Fewer wildcard chains, but much slower contact and more playing inside existing land.

variants.name: Four spread jokers
variants.review: Not a clear improvement on the large board; attacks fall and contact comes later.

variants.name: Eight spread jokers
variants.review: Makes contact easy but strongly encourages wildcard-heavy words.

variants.name: Six jokers, neutral ones near centre
variants.review: Clustered central wildcards create an express route and frequent multi-joker words.

variants.name: Four central jokers, none at home
variants.review: Central concentration drives contact, but wildcards dominate routes and skilled-model seat bias is concerning.

variants.name: At most one joker per word
variants.review: Reduces chains at the price of a new restriction and less interaction.

variants.name: Vowel target 42%
variants.review: Potential word-finding comfort improvement; does not by itself create a stronger territory trade-off.

variants.name: 45-tile board
variants.review: Fast contact, but six jokers are dense on 45 tiles.

variants.name: 160-letter budget
variants.review: More time to fight, at the cost of a substantially longer asynchronous commitment.

variants.name: Only captured letters refresh
variants.review: Reduced letter churn did not improve territory sacrifices; repetition remains an exploit concern to test further.

variants.name: Three central castles worth 5
variants.review: Readable objectives, but central placement alone did not improve limited-attention choices.

variants.name: 12-point central-castle majority
variants.review: Creates a target but risks a final-turn jackpot and another scoring rule.

variants.name: Land 2 / castles 5 + four jokers
variants.review: Higher land values work, but fewer jokers slow the large board.

variants.name: Castle holding + four jokers
variants.review: Combines reduced contact with recurring income; not the strongest next test.

variants.name: Territory matures after a held round
variants.review: Best non-recurring holding prototype: fresh land 1/3, mature land 2/5 after a full round. Adds state to explain.

variants.name: Six spaced bridge jokers
variants.review: Spaced neutral jokers modestly speed contact, but increase multi-joker use.

variants.name: Land 2 / castles 5 + bridge jokers
variants.review: Promising interaction, but change scoring and placement separately before combining.

variants.name: Castle hold earns 3 once per player
variants.review: A bounded defense reward: only about 6% of scores, but modest behavior change.

variants.name: Held castles earn 1, capped at 2
variants.review: If recurring rewards are desired, a restrained option: +1 per held castle, at most 2 per round.

variants.name: 45-tile board with four jokers
variants.review: Best board-layout playtest: 45 tiles with four jokers; earlier contact without dense wildcard chains.

variants.name: 12 rounds instead of letter budget
variants.review: More predictable turns, but a different time commitment depending on word-finding skill.

variants.name: Jokers become letters after use
variants.review: Interesting one-use exploration boost; opening depletion and first-player effects need work.

variants.name: At most two jokers per word
variants.review: Small impact for the limited-attention model; a new rule without a strong measured benefit.

variants.name: Central castles + four frontier jokers
variants.review: Many fights, but extreme wildcard concentration masks ordinary word finding.
